title: unified-api-observability-add-requestid-trace-propagation-and-per-endpoint-metrics-tags
author: Lina Chen
release_notes: Added request id + trace propagation across API surface, structured logs with request/trace fields, per-endpoint metrics tags, and OpenAI-compatibility header mapping. No user-visible breaking changes; opt-in header behavior documented.
description:
Motivation: Production incidents and customer feedback showed gaps in observability across the public API surface: missing/unstable request ids for streaming responses, inconsistent trace propagation through the OpenAI compatibility layer, and insufficient per-endpoint metric tags for cost/latency attribution. This PR adds a unified request ID and trace propagation model, structured JSON logging augmentation, and per-endpoint metrics tags so latency/cost dashboards and alerting can attribute behavior correctly.

What this change does (summary): - Assigns a stable request_id at the API ingress for every request (hosted/dedicated/private). The request_id is included as: X-Request-Id response header, a top-level field in structured JSON logs (request_id), and injected into streaming chunk envelopes so that partial responses can be correlated to a single request. - Propagates tracing headers (traceparent and b3 where present) to internal services and exporters; integrates with our OpenTelemetry pipeline. We canonicalize trace ids to trace_id in structured logs. - Enhances the OpenAI compatibility layer: preserve incoming OpenAI-style request ids (if present) and map them onto internal request_id while returning OpenAI-compatible response ids; ensure the x-request-id header is forwarded and mirrored to openai response 'id'. - Adds per-endpoint and per-model metric tags (route, operation, model.family) emitted to metrics backend so dashboards can slice latency and token cost by API route (completion/chat/embeddings), model family, and plan tier. - Structured log fields: request_id, trace_id, route, http_method, user_id (when present), model, tokens_in, tokens_out, response_status, tool_call_id (for function/tool calls). - Streaming stability changes: ensure server assigns request_id before handshake completes with client; streaming chunks now include metadata envelopes with request_id and sequence numbers. This reduces misattribution for aborted/partial streams. - Function/tool calling observability: each tool call receives a tool_call_id and is correlated to the parent request trace; logs include tool_call_id/tool_name and duration. - Tests and CI: unit tests for header mapping, integration tests for streaming chunk envelopes, and a smoke test to validate metrics tags are emitted.

Design notes: - We intentionally keep the internal canonical ID as rr_request_id but expose it as X-Request-Id for HTTP compatibility and map it to OpenAI 'id' when using the compatibility endpoint. This avoids breaking customers who rely on existing OpenAI response id semantics while giving internal services a consistent key. - Trace propagation supports both W3C traceparent and B3. When both are present we prefer W3C and log both in debug mode. Traces are exported via our existing Otel collector config; no schema changes to the tracing backend. - Metrics tag cardinality is constrained: model.family is used rather than full model version in high-cardinality metrics. Route is normalized (chat.completions -> chat, completions -> completion, embeddings -> embedding). - Streaming envelope format: each chunk begins with a lightweight JSON prefix: {"request_id":"...","seq":42,"trace_id":"..."} followed by payload. The prefix is base64-safe and parsed by our SDKs; fallback behavior: legacy clients ignoring the prefix still receive the payload uninterrupted (we validated parsing safety).

Files changed (high level): - api/gateway/handler.go: assign request_id early, header mapping, trace extraction. - api/gateway/streaming.go: chunk envelope implementation and handshake update. - compat/openai/translator.go: map x-request-id <-> openai id and ensure streaming envelope compatibility. - runtime/observability/logging.go: structured logger helpers and keys. - runtime/observability/metrics.go: metric tag extraction and emission code, tag normalization helpers. - runtime/tooling/tool-calls.go: tool_call_id generation and correlation instrumentation. - integration_tests/test_observability_streaming.py: end-to-end streaming + header assertions. - unit_tests/test_openai_compat_header_mapping.go: mapping edge cases. - docs/api/observability.md: new docs section explaining headers, logs, and metric tags.

Commits (summary): - 0a3d8f2: initial gateway instrumentation and request id generation - 3b9f1c7: implement streaming chunk envelopes and SDK-friendly prefix - b1e4c6a: add OpenAI compatibility header mapping and translator tests - 6f7d2a1: structured logger helpers and trace canonicalization - f2c11b9: metrics tags emission and normalization + unit tests - 9d2b4e0: tool calling instrumentation and tool_call_id propagation - a7e8f33: docs and changelog entry; added rollout plan

Testing and CI notes: - Initial CI run had an intermittent failure in streaming integration (integration_tests/test_observability_streaming.py) due to race on request_id injection; fixed by ensuring request_id is assigned before stream handshake completes and adding a short synchronization point in the test harness. - All unit tests + integration tests passing after fixes; end-to-end smoke run on staging validated traces appear in OTEL backend with correct trace_id and request_id tags, and metrics dashboard received route/model tags. CI status: pass.

Review conversation (high level): - Miguel Alvarez: "Can we avoid increasing tag cardinality for metrics? We should prefer model.family not full model names." Author reply: "Agree — changed emission to use model.family for high volume metrics; full model appears only in debug traces." - Priya Nair: "Will OpenAI compat clients see any header changes?" Author reply: "No breaking change. We mirror internal rr_request_id to openai 'id' and return X-Request-Id as before. We document a new X-Redwood-Request-Id alias for debug." - Evan Brooks: "Streaming envelope looks good. Make sure SDKs handle prefix safely." Author reply: "Added parsing helpers in SDK interface and verified TS+Python SDK unit tests in their repos in follow-up PRs." - QA (Marcos): "Observed a case where aborted streams left dangling metrics. Can you increment a 'stream.aborted' metric?" Author reply: "Added stream.aborted counter emitted when connection closed before final chunk; included in metrics change set."

Backward compatibility and rollout: - Backwards compatible by default. Legacy clients that ignore the chunk envelope still receive payload; envelopes are designed to be safely ignored if not parsed. - Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime flag. Step 1: deploy to staging and run smoke tests (done). Step 2: deploy to canary subset of Hosted API (5% traffic) for 24 hours and monitor error/latency/trace correspondence dashboards. Step 3: full rollout with a 1h pause and rollback criteria defined in docs. We used canary run results to validate no increase in tail latency.

Operational impact and alerts: - New dashboards added: API Request ID heatmap, Route x Model latency with request_id tagging, Streaming chunk success rate. - Alerts: increase in stream.aborted > 0.5% over baseline, mismatch count where request_id missing in logs > 0.1% of requests, and drop in trace sampling/ingestion.

Follow-ups and TODOs: - SDK PRs to consume streaming prefix and surface request_id in client logs (TS+Python open follow-up PRs). - Instrument cost attribution pipeline to use model.family metric tags for billing experiments. - Add optional opt-out header X-Redwood-No-Request-Id for customers with specific privacy constraints (follow-up RFC).

Summary: This PR improves end-to-end observability of Redwood's API surface by unifying request IDs, ensuring trace propagation throughout the stack, adding structured logs and per-endpoint metric tags, and keeping compatibility with OpenAI-style clients. The change was reviewed, tested, and merged (squash merge) to main on 2026-02-23.
